python3 -c "
# In obs 33:
# Center u = 244.5, v_bottom = 479
# Distance zc = 1.779
# Radius of cylinder in 3D:
# width in pixels = 277 - 212 = 65 pixels
# 65 * 1.779 / 256 = 0.45m diameter -> radius R ~ 0.225m
# The bottom visible arc in perspective projection contacts floor at z = z_center - R? Or z_center?
# For a vertical cylinder of radius R:
# The bottom profile touches the floor. The front-most point of the bottom rim is at z = z_center - R!
# So z_center = z_contact + R!
# At heading 120°:
# Robot pose: (-0.634, 3.866)
# If front contact is at (0.947, 3.046), then center along line of sight (heading 120°) is:
# center = (0.947 + 0.225 * sin(120°), 3.046 + 0.225 * cos(120°))
# = (0.947 + 0.195, 3.046 - 0.112) = (1.142, 2.934)!
# Look at obs 1 base world: (1.086, 2.699) -> front contact along heading 0° (along +y) was at y=2.699!
# Then center is at y = 2.699 + R = 2.699 + 0.225 = 2.924, x = 1.086!
# Look at obs 6 base world: (1.068, 2.704) -> center at y = 2.704 + 0.225 = 2.929, x = 1.068!
# Look at obs 32 base world: (0.947, 3.038) -> heading 90° (along +x). Front contact at x = 0.947!
# Then center along +x is at x = 0.947 + 0.225 = 1.172, y = 3.038!
# They ALL CONVERGE to the exact same 3D cylinder center:
# x ~ 1.10, y ~ 2.95!
print('Exact center convergence:')
print(f'From obs 1 (heading 0): x=1.086, y={2.699+0.225:.3f}')
print(f'From obs 6 (heading 0): x=1.068, y={2.704+0.225:.3f}')
print(f'From obs 32 (heading 90): x={0.947+0.225:.3f}, y=3.038')
print(f'From obs 33 (heading 120): x={0.947+0.225*math.sin(math.radians(120)):.3f}, y={3.046+0.225*math.cos(math.radians(120)):.3f}')
"
